newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares fall in nervous trade, ITC tumbles.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares fall in nervous trade, ITC tumbles.

text.p: Indian shares fell sharply on Wednesday rocked by rumours the enforcement directorate had arrested top ITC officials, brokers said.

The Finance Ministry said in the evening the enforcement agency arrested a director of the tobacco conglomerate and three former employees on alleged violation of foreign exchange rules in export deals.

Senior ITC officials have been accused of violations of India's Foreign Exchange Regulation Act in connection with some of the firm's export deals. ITC share fell 18.25 rupees, or 5.68 percent, to 303 at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
ITC is 31.7 percent controlled by Britain's B.A.T. Industries Plc.
The government statement said the authorities raided the company's premises and the homes of its directors in Calcutta, Delhi, Bombay and Hyderabad.
"The search operations were organised ...(on documentary evidence of foreign exchange violations) to the tune of $100 million," the statement released in New Delhi said.
Brokers said the enforcement raid talk triggered speculative selling pressure and unnerved players.
The 30-share BSE index ended 66.96 points, or 2.07 percent, lower at 3,172.98 after sliding to 3,163.40.

The 500-stock CRISIL index finished 9.00 points, or 1.45 percent, lower at 610.76. The Delhi index shed 7.50 points to 731.39, the Calcutta index 3.61 points to 430.70 and the Madras index 10.89 points to 3,262.33.
There was no trading at the National exchange due to a technical snag but it will resume dealings on Thursday, the bourse said.
Thermax edged up 0.75 rupees to 346.75 after it said first half net profit rose 31 percent to 199.2 million rupees.
